extra.//ios.infoPlist.NSAppTransportSecurity: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads stays true on purpose, and this is the App Review answer. Muqun is a developer tool that only ever talks to a Gateway the user runs on their own computer; the user types or scans that address, and a bare host is normalised to http:// (src/lib/pairing.ts). Those hosts are LAN or Tailscale tailnet addresses with no public DNS name and no CA-issued certificate, so TLS is not available to pin against. NSAllowsLocalNetworking is also set, but it only exempts unqualified names, .local and the reserved local ranges -- it does not cover the 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT space Tailscale hands out, so it cannot replace arbitrary loads here. No traffic goes to an Osuki server; there is no relay, no analytics and no ad network. HTTPS is used whenever the user's Gateway offers it (Tailscale Serve).
extra.//ios.infoPlist.ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncry: TODO before shipping the SSH client (feature/ssh-client): `false` is left as it was, and it is no longer obviously right. @osuki-dev/react-native-ssh links its own SSH implementation (russh on aws-lc), which is proprietary-to-the-app encryption in App Store Connect's terms rather than a use of the OS's TLS -- the exemption this answer relied on. Before the next submission with the SSH entry in the build, decide the export classification: most likely `true` plus the self-classification report (SSH is a standard protocol, so the 5D992 mass-market / EAR 740.17(b)(1) route applies, and the annual self-classification report to BIS/NSA is the app owner's to file), or a documented case that the exemption still holds. The gateway transport is unaffected: its AES-GCM sits on the same footing it always did.
extra.//ios.privacyManifests: Audited against the prebuilt Pods, not guessed. Declared: UserDefaults CA92.1 (expo-updates UpdatesConfigOverride.swift and react-native-nitro-fetch read/write app-private defaults) and 1C8F.1 (expo-widgets WidgetsStorage.swift writes the group.dev.osuki.muqun suite the widget extension reads); FileTimestamp C617.1 (MMKVCore MemoryFile.cpp calls stat/fstat on its own container files and ships no PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy). NOT declared: SystemBootTime 35F9.1 and DiskSpace E174.1/85F4.1 -- the only callers are expo-device and expo-file-system, which ship their own privacy manifests as pod resource bundles; FileTimestamp DDA9.1 -- the file times shown in the files sheet arrive from the Gateway over HTTP, no iOS file API is called to read them.
